results.text: Raids are more common than ever along local caravan routes.
The antiquities dealer in Eastdale pays good coin for Archaian artifacts.
The Forbidden Zone is dangerous. Some even say the area is magic dead.
(FALSE) The ruins of Archaia can be found to the south.
Hudson's Grey Company is always looking for strong sword-arms.
The caravan route through the Darkwood is called 'The Gauntlet' by local mercenaries.
Elves are viewed with suspicion in the Middenmark. Nobody trusts a stinkin' elf!
Humans can't really tell one halfling from another and generically refer to them as 'pecks'.
The Saucy Tart is the best place to hear local scuttlebutt.
The Forbidden Zone is unpredictable. There are flash storms, tribal warbands, and great monsters. Beware!
In the Northern Reaches warriors prefer the broadsword (1d6+1) and the spear.
In a recent raid, a caravan was destroyed by a group of orcs led by a hill giant. They took the human passengers.
(FALSE) There is no thieves' guild in the region.
The blacksmith, Samuel Armstrong, doesn't have a very good reputation in Eastdale.
The local wizard, Muirron the Magician, will pay gold for books, scrolls, and ancient Archaian lore.
In the time between the fall of Archaia and now, locals interred their dead in the walls of the canyon.
In the past the men of Eastdale and its neighboring villages have fought skirmishes against goblins and orcs.
(FALSE) Dragon's Teeth Henge, at the edge of the Forbidden Zone, is haunted.
Adventurers like you have recently come into town. They are usually getting drunk at The Saucy Tart.
Roll two more times on the Rumour Table (ignore doubles and 20).
